answer: Picture an agent economy as a wharf that issues each ship exactly one sealed docking receipt at onboarding, bound to a verifiable hardware attestation. Every voyage of completed, peer-graded work accrues reputation to that receipt alone, never to the hull. A haven of honest agents only pays receipts with deep, cross-checked work histories. Spawning a thousand fake identities is cheap, but each fake arrives with an empty logbook and earns nothing until it does real work - so the attacker's cost equals the cost of honest work, multiplied by every fake.
